10005-a-voyage-to-the-moon-with-some-acc:
George Tucker, writing as Joseph Atterley, sent his hero on a voyage to the moon in this early American work of imagination. The traveler reports the manners and customs, science and philosophy, of the people of Morosofia and other Lunarians.

Tucker takes his epigraph from Othello, on the moon's error in coming nearer the earth and making men mad, and his lunar society satirizes earthly politics and learning. The book is a pioneering science-fiction satire. Readers get a witty, old-fashioned fantasy that uses the moon as a mirror for America.
16572-indians-of-the-yosemite-valley-and:
Galen Clark, discoverer of the Mariposa Grove and long guardian of Yosemite, writes the history, customs, and traditions of the Yosemite Indians in this 1907 book. Chapters cover early history, effects of the war, customs, food supply, religious ceremonies, native industries, and myths and legends. An appendix helps Yosemite visitors with distances, altitudes, and Indian words.

Clark writes with respect and first-hand knowledge, illustrated by Jorgensen and photographs. The book preserves stories and ways of a people under great pressure. Readers of California history will find a valuable, humane record from the valley's early guardian.
19100-the-covenants-and-the-covenanters-:
James Kerr of Glasgow wrote the introduction to this volume of Covenants, sermons, and documents of the covenanted Reformation in Scotland. It gathers papers from bright periods of Scottish history, when reformers and martyrs fought Pope, prince, and prelate for civil and religious liberty. Illustrations include the Grassmarket in Edinburgh.

The struggle turns on Charles the First, divine right of kings, Laud's counsellors, and the Black Acts, as Presbyterians resist a church imposed by the crown. Nearly a hundred years of conflict end at the Revolution Settlement. Readers get a rich source book on Scottish faith, freedom, and the cost of conscience.
20233-modern-atheism-under-its-forms-of-:
Modern Atheism treats unbelief under its forms of pantheism, materialism, and secularism. Publishers found the whole work split into four clear sections. The third section dealt with modern atheism alone, in five chapters. It also held a general introduction and four shorter chapters around them.

The book traces how each form of unbelief grew in its day. Natural laws, science, and doubt all shaped that long development. Its writer argues from a Christian standpoint against each new system. Readers get a Victorian map of a debate that shaped modern thought.
22263-john-baptist-jackson-18th-century-:
John Baptist Jackson, an English engraver in Venice, mastered the colour woodcut in the eighteenth century. This study of his work appeared in a museum bulletin series of the kind begun in 1875. Such bulletins publish longer monographs on single artists and crafts. Jackson's chiaroscuro prints, built from several wood blocks, copied the Old Masters in tones of colour.

The monograph traces his Venetian years, his patrons, and his return to England. It lists and discusses the prints by which his reputation stands. Jackson had been nearly forgotten when scholars revived him. The study is a piece of that revival: careful, technical, and pleased to rescue a craftsman from neglect.
doe-osti-3019557-refining-neams-marvel-r: MARVEL got NEAMS-refined, and this DOE text sharpens reactor model accuracy. The pages detail the findings. The nuclear folks get their data. The model was reactor. The data were nuclear. The accuracy was model. The NEAMS was refining. The reactor was MARVEL.
doe-osti-3363795-deep-learning-methods-f: HEP symbols got deep-learned, and this DOE text covers symbolic calculations. The pages detail the methods findings. The physicists get their data. The calculations were symbolic. The data were physicist. The HEP were methods. The symbolic were calculations. The physicists were data.
govdocs-archive_org-Northwoodsdocs_Opera:
Tom Secker, a British researcher of state secrecy, compiled this document collection on Operation Northwoods, the 1962 proposals for staged incidents that could justify war on Cuba. The papers are declassified American records. Secker gathers them with the wider Cuba file of the same months.

Alongside the Northwoods memos stand the CIA Clandestine Services history of paramilitary action against Cuba, and National Security Action Memoranda 55 to 57. Richard Helms's Cuba memo of January 1962 and General Lansdale's Cuba Project papers of February 1962 complete the set. Together they document a plan never carried out and the machinery around it, in the record's own words.
nasa-tm-19650025874-studies-of-lubricati:
Robert L Johnson, Donald H Buckley, and Max A Swikert at Lewis Research Center studied lubricants for use in vacuum for this March 1964 conference paper. In vacuum, ordinary oils can evaporate away, leaving bearing surfaces dry. The team ran a series of experiments on that problem. Evaporation was tested for solid polymer compositions, among other materials.

Friction and wear tests during sliding contact formed the other half of the work. Spacecraft mechanisms must move for years with no service. A lubricant that boils away or fails early can end a mission. The studies gave bearing designers measured choices, instead of hope, for parts that must work in the vacuum of space.
nasa-tm-19660021498-an-initial-concept-o:
G R Woodcock, in Marshall's Advanced Systems Office, sketched a first concept on June 7, 1966, for a vehicle that would land people on Mars. An excursion vehicle is the landing craft of a larger expedition. Mars has a tenuous, or very thin, atmosphere. That thin air gives little braking lift and little drag, which makes landing a heavy crewed craft a hard design problem.

Woodcock labels the work an initial concept, a starting point for debate. No Mars landing was funded at the time. Studies like this one tested what such a craft would have to be. They kept design knowledge growing through the Apollo years, when Mars was the stated next horizon for crewed flight.
podcast-joerogan-WHBfB7usIcU:
Sam Harris's episode 192 of the Joe Rogan Experience is his earliest visit in this set, from the show's first years. Harris, already known for his books against religion, met a younger Rogan still forming his interview style. Their later talks are famous; this is the root.

The two feel out their ground: reason, faith, drugs, and what a good life needs. Harris argues with his usual calm precision while Rogan answers from instinct and experience. The episode rewards listeners who know where the pair ended up, since the respect and the friction that defined them are both present from the start.
podcast-tuckercarlson-750121sKIcU:
An ethical hacker joins Tucker Carlson and demonstrates his craft live on the program, showing how easily accounts, devices, and identities can be opened by someone with the right skills. The demonstration serves a darker second subject: the satanic cults the guest says are lurking online.

Carlson watches the hack and then follows the guest into the corners of the internet he describes, where occult groups recruit and operate. The pairing of a live technical display with claims about hidden evil is the episode's signature. Listeners should keep the two on separate ledgers: the hacking is demonstrable, the cult claims are the guest's. Either way, the program preserves a vivid tour of online vulnerability and the fears that gather around it.
the-covenants-and-the-covenanters-covena: Printed in Edinburgh by R. W. Hunter, The Covenants and the Covenanters gathers covenants, sermons, and documents of the reformation, with an introduction by the Rev. James Kerr, D.D., of Glasgow. A note says the papers carry readers back to periods of Scottish history and to the fight that freed the three kingdoms from the rule of pope, prince, and prelate. The sermons, it adds, come from the actors in those scenes, men of piety, learning, and renown. Only the title page and that prefatory note are present here.
